Log look plain text, ISO8601 UTC timestamp, level tag INFO/WARN/ERROR fixed-width. No script/locale/unit weirdness.

1. SURFACE: Plaintext server log, one line per event. Timestamp ISO8601 with Z (UTC). Level field padded (`ERROR`, `INFO `, `WARN `). key=value fields after message. ASCII, LF lines presumably.

2. CONTENT: Matches surface — straightforward level-tagged log, no encoding/locale tricks. Level string literally `ERROR` (all caps, no variants like `Error`/`ERR`/`error` seen in sample, but 5210 lines total, only 8 shown — can't rule out variant casing or `ERR` abbreviation existing elsewhere).
CONTENT VERDICT: NO MISMATCH

3. MISREADINGS:
- Grep `ERROR` case-sensitive vs case-insensitive: fine here since sample all-caps, but if log has mixed case elsewhere, counts differ. Evidence: sample shows only uppercase `ERROR`.
- Matching literal string `ERROR` anywhere in line vs only in level field: message text could contain word "error" elsewhere (e.g. `msg="rate error"` under INFO) causing overcount if not anchored to level column. Evidence: sample lines have level as 2nd whitespace-token after timestamp — safer to match that field specifically.
- WARN lines mistaken as errors (severity conflation) — not seen in sample but common mistake. Evidence: WARN distinct tag, task explicit says ERROR only.
- Multi-line stack traces (continuation lines w/o own timestamp) under one ERROR — could undercount or overcount if each physical line counted vs each log event. Sample has no multi-line entries, but 5210-line file unseen majority could. Can't confirm/deny from sample alone.
- Line count encoding: counting `\n` occurrences vs actual log lines — fine if file well-formed, but trailing newline / blank lines could skew off-by-one. Not evidenced in sample.
